theater: 交趾、鬱林間的嶺南山地

battle.name: 馬援征嶺南之戰
battle.theater: 交趾、鬱林間的嶺南山地
battle.brief: 建武十六年秋，交趾校尉李贄與陳濤起兵反漢，殺太守，鬱林、桂林諸郡兵隨之響應。詔以伏波將軍馬援將兵南下，溯湘江、漓江入鬱林，再沿水路直抵交趾，翌年擒斬首謀，復置郡縣與屯田。卡面的希臘重步兵不在嶺南，它點出的是同一道理：盾牆能擋住衝鋒，靠的是成陣而非個人。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 交戰一方是東漢朝廷，另一方是起兵反亂的交趾叛軍與響應的南疆郡縣。建武十六年秋，交州所屬交趾郡最先出事：校尉李贄與陳濤舉兵，殺死交趾太守，郡兵隨之而反，鬱林、桂林、南海、合浦各郡先後響應，叛軍據交趾城與交趾北面的山嶺、溪谷為據，號令及於鬱林一帶，構成一次以郡兵為骨幹、以越人諸部為補充的地方性反亂。朝廷方面由光武帝下詔，徵大將軍馬援以伏波將軍之號統兵討之；中樞尚書臺議定方略後，兵權集中於主將一身，馬援全權調度沿線郡兵並節制交州各太守，事平之後交州才正式歸入刺史部的統一編制。東漢出兵的結構是徵發與募取並用：北軍與中央宿衛為骨干，配荊州、桂陽、零陵、鬱林、桂林諸郡的郡兵、鄉勇，以及熟悉嶺南山道水路的嚮導；後勤則幾乎全靠內地供給，糧秣、器械、藥物沿湘江—漓江—珠江水系與陸路北運，沿海一段靠合浦、南海的鹽與粟米以及民間船戶的協運。整場戰爭的實質，是中央能不能把兵、糧與秩序一起送下五嶺之南。
countriesEn: One side was the court of the Eastern Han, the other the troops of Jiaozhi in revolt together with the southern commanderies that joined them. In the autumn of the sixteenth year of Jianwu, the disturbance began in Jiaozhi, a commandery of Jiaozhou: the commandant Li Zhi and Chen Tao raised troops, killed the Administrator of Jiaozhi, and the commandery soldiers followed them into rebellion. Yulin, Guilin, Nanhai and Hepu answered in turn, and the insurgents held the city of Jiaozhi together with the ridges and gullies to the north of it, their orders reaching as far as the Yulin region. What they built was a local rising with commandery troops as its backbone and the local Yue bands as auxiliaries. On the other side, Emperor Guangwu of the Eastern Han issued the edict that summoned the General-in-Chief Ma Yuan, who marched as Fubo General; the Bureau of Documents settled the plan, and command then concentrated in the hands of the field commander. Ma Yuan was given full authority to move the commandery troops along the route and to control the administrators of the Jiaozhou commanderies, and only after the affair was over did Jiaozhou pass formally under the unified command of the Inspectorate. The Han force combined levies with volunteers: the Northern Army and the central palace guard formed the core, joined by commandery troops, local braves and guides from the commanderies of Jingzhou, Guiyang, Lingling, Yulin and Guilin, and by men who knew the mountain paths and the waterways of Lingnan. The rear areas were supplied almost entirely from the interior; grain, equipment and medicine moved south by the Xiang, Li and Zhu river systems and by road, while along the coast the salt and rice of Hepu and Nanhai and the help of local boat families did much of the work. In its essentials, this war asked whether the centre could deliver troops, grain and order together, all the way south of the Five Ranges.
people: 主將馬援，字文淵，陝西扶風茂陵人，東漢開國名將，出仕前已在涼州羌地與北方邊線上屢建戰功，官至大將軍。他兩度經營羌事，屢辭朝廷優厚之命而求外任；建武十六年交趾反亂時，正是他自請南征，其上疏中「大丈夫當立功異域，以覩天子之德」一類言語，成為日後史書講述遠征時最常被引用的句子。叛方首謀是交趾校尉李贄，同謀者陳濤；反亂發動後，交趾太守遇害，其名諱在《後漢書》與《資治通鑑》的敘述中未見詳載。朝廷中枢的決策者是光武帝劉秀，他接到奏報後詔令出兵，並在是否先撫後討、抑或徑行討伐之間作過衡量，最終以大軍進剿收局。越人諸部的首領在本戰的記載中多不具名，只以「越人」「南蠻」或「叟、俚」之類的群體稱呼出現，這既反映當時史官對嶺南地方勢力的記錄有限，也意味著推動叛亂的社會基礎比幾個名字所能涵蓋的更廣。馬援本人於建武二十五年（公元49年）卒，壽三十六歲；他死後詔令史官為之立傳，其生平與此役的細節主要就靠這部後來收進《後漢書》的傳記保存下來。
peopleEn: The commander was Ma Yuan, courtesy name Wenyuan, a native of Maoling in Fufeng in Shaanxi and one of the founding generals of the Eastern Han, who before taking office had already served repeatedly on the Qiang frontier of Liangzhou, and who rose to the rank of General-in-Chief. He fought the Qiang more than once, and refused the generous rewards the court offered him more than once in order to be posted abroad; when Jiaozhi rose in the sixteenth year of Jianwu, it was he who volunteered for the southern command, and the sentence in his memorial about a great man earning his achievement in a distant land and beholding the virtue of the Son of Heaven became the line most often quoted afterwards when historians wrote about far-off expeditions. The leader of the rising was Li Zhi, commandant of Jiaozhi, with Chen Tao as his accomplice. Once it had begun, the Administrator of Jiaozhi was killed, and his name is not given in detail either in the History of the Later Han or in the Comprehensive Mirror. The decision at the centre was taken by Emperor Guangwu, Liu Xiu, who issued the orders to send troops and who weighed whether to pacify first and punish afterwards or to strike at once, ending by choosing the outright campaign. The chiefs of the Yue bands are mostly nameless in the record of this war, appearing only as collective labels such as Yue people, Southern Man, or the Sou and Li groups; that reflects how thin the Han historians' information about local southern power was, and it also means that the social base of the revolt was broader than any handful of names. Ma Yuan died in the twenty-fifth year of Jianwu, in 49 AD, aged thirty-six. After his death an edict ordered the court historiographers to compose his biography, and it is chiefly through that biography, later incorporated into the History of the Later Han, that the details of his life and of this campaign have come down to us.
kits: 卡面這名希臘重步兵並不屬於東漢軍制，也沒有出現在嶺南的任何記載中；它是一件對照件，用來比照東漢甲士結陣時的同一套道理。真正投入這場戰爭的，是中原與江南的典型漢軍裝備：步行作戰的甲士穿札甲、戴冑，持環首刀、長劍、矛與戟，正面用蒙皮大盾遮蔽；弩手以臂弩、蹶張弩施放矢，與持盾甲士搭配，構成遠射在前、刀盾在後的組合；大型的床弩、撞車與雲梯則留給攻交趾城牆之用。希臘重步兵的價值，在於它點明方陣的支點是互相遮蔽而非個人勇力；東漢甲士在山林中結陣抵擋叛軍衝鋒，用的是同一個原理，只是破陣的火力由弩砲提供，而不是靠撞盾頂住對方的重步兵。叛軍那邊的器材，多取自郡縣武庫與越地所產：長刀、弓弩、藤盾與竹木自製的矛梃，並依山就險築木寨、伐木為柵，憑險阻水而守。運輸方面，湘江、漓江、珠江與交趾水道一線用的是漢軍船型（樓船、走舸、斗艦一類的舊制）加上竹筏與自備小艇，輜重車、牛、馬則在陸路與水陸轉接處使用。軍中還備有柴薪與火炬，供夜襲與火攻之需。
kitsEn: The Greek hoplite on the card belongs to no Han order of battle and appears in no record of Lingnan; it is a comparison piece, set there to illustrate the same principle that governed how Han armoured infantry closed ranks. What actually went into this war was the standard Han equipment of the central plain and the south: foot soldiers in lamellar armour and helmets, carrying ring-pommel sabres, swords, spears and halberds, with a hide-covered large shield masking the front; crossbowmen working light crossbows and spring-driven tension bows, paired with the shield-bearers so that missile fire came first and sabre and shield followed; and the heavy crossbows, battering rams and scaling ladders held back for the assault on the walls of Jiaozhi. The hoplite's worth lies in the point it makes: the strength of a phalanx rests on mutual cover rather than on individual valour. Han armoured infantry holding their ranks in the forest against the insurgents' charges used the same logic, except that the breaking force was supplied by the crossbows rather than by shield against shield. The rebels drew their gear from the commandery armouries and from what the south produced: long sabres, bows and crossbows, rattan shields, spears and javelins of bamboo and wood, and they built stockades and felled trees for barriers, holding ground on heights and blocking the watercourses. On the transport side, the Han force used the ship types of Han practice along the Xiang, Li and Zhu rivers and the waterways of Jiaozhi — the old tower-ships, light galleys and fighting barges — supplemented by bamboo rafts and private small boats, while baggage carts, draught oxen and horses served the land route and the transshipment points between land and water. Firewood and torches were carried in the train as well, for night attacks and for burning.
tactics: 這場戰役的大戰略是由北而南、順水而下：先取鬱林，切斷叛軍與交趾之間的聯繫與糧道，再循江溯流直抵交趾。隊伍自湘鄉一帶集結，沿湘江經零陵、桂陽、桂林南下，轉入漓江與鬱江水路，最後沿交趾的水道逼近叛軍核心。推進過程中，馬援沒有把全軍壓成一條隊形縱隊，而是分兵：一支隨江順流作正面進攻，一支緣山嶺疾進，尋山路迂迴到叛軍側背；沿途據險立營，置烽燧守道，保住糧道不斷。接戰時先用弩矢遠射擾亂守軍的陣腳，再以騎兵衝其側翼，待敵陣亂才以甲士結陣進逼，長兵器在前、短兵在後，穩步壓上。遇到依山阻水、築寨固守的守軍，則以火攻與夜襲破之：南方山林柴薪易得，焚燒寨栅能逼守軍離開遮蔽；追擊殘部時則循溪谷搜剿，並斷其水源與田禾，逼其無糧可守。攻城一段用撞車破門、雲梯登城，弩手在梯旁掩護，攻梯的將士才不致被城頭直射壓死。最後一點也最實際：這支遠征軍的勝負，很大程度上由糧秣供應與疫病管理決定，而不是由某一次會戰的陣形決定。
tacticsEn: The grand strategy of this campaign was to move from north to south, downstream with the current: take Yulin first, cutting the rebels' link and supply route to Jiaozhi, and then follow the river up to strike at Jiaozhi itself. The column assembled in the neighbourhood of Xiangxiang, moved down the Xiang River past Lingling, Guiyang and Guilin, turned onto the Li and Yu waterways, and closed on the rebel core along the waters of Jiaozhi. Ma Yuan did not push the whole army forward as a single column. He split it: one part moved with the river on the front, one part struck along the ridges to find a mountain path and come round onto the rebels' flank and rear, and the line entrenched on heights as it advanced, with beacon towers and fortified posts guarding the road so that the supply line never broke. In contact, crossbow volleys went in first to disturb the defenders' formation, cavalry struck the flanks, and only then did the armoured infantry close up in ranks, long weapons forward and short weapons behind, advancing in step. Where the enemy held ground on heights and barricaded the watercourses behind timber stockades, the answer was fire and night attack: in the southern forests firewood was abundant, and burning the palisades forced the defenders out of their cover. Pursuit was carried out along the gullies and streams, the water sources and standing crops being cut off so that the fugitives had no grain to sit on. At the walls, battering rams were used against the gates and scaling ladders went up under the covering fire of crossbowmen, who kept the defenders' direct fire off the men on the ladders. The last point is also the most practical: the outcome of this distant expedition was decided far more by the supply of grain and by the management of sickness than by the formation used in any single engagement.
data: 可以核實的數字不多，記錄本身就相當簡略。時間上：建武十六年（公元40年）秋，叛亂起；同年九月前後朝廷發兵；建武十七年（公元41年）交趾平定，全程約一年上下。距離上：自湘鄉集結地順水至交趾，行程二千餘里，合今一千公里以上，路上要經湘江、漓江、珠江與交趾水道四段水系，換船、屯兵、轉運糧秣的次數都由此決定。兵力上：史籍未載確數，只知是一支多郡募兵與徵調兵混編的部隊，其中原籍中原本部為骨干，南方郡兵擔任嚮導與補充；可以確定它具備分兵、據險與攻城同時進行的規模，否則無法在一年之內走完這條線。叛軍方面同樣沒有確數，只知是郡兵為主幹、附以越人諸部的武裝，人數足以據山阻江、築寨固守，也足以在野戰中被討平。傷亡與斬獲，各家記載互有出入而不可考，可信的是：首謀李贄被斬，陳濤所部隨之潰散，交州各郡相繼歸附，戰果的形式是斬首若干與降附若干，而不是一場全殲的會戰。行政上，交州之下交趾、鬱林、桂林、南海、合浦五郡的地方建制在戰後重新接回朝廷，縣、亭、屯田與鎮兵隨之恢復；沿海的合浦、南海是當時重要的鹽產地，鹽與粟米是遠征軍在海岸段最依賴的物資。
dataEn: Few numbers can be verified, because the record itself is thin. On timing: the rising began in the autumn of the sixteenth year of Jianwu, in 40 AD; troops were dispatched around the ninth month of that year; Jiaozhi was pacified in the seventeenth year of Jianwu, in 41 AD, so the whole business took roughly a year. On distance: from the assembly point at Xiangxiang down the water to Jiaozhi is more than two thousand li, over a thousand kilometres today, and the line crosses four separate water systems in succession — the Xiang, the Li, the Zhu and the waterways of Jiaozhi — which fixes the number of times the column had to change boats, halt to refit, and shift its grain. On numbers of troops: the histories give no exact figure, only that this was a mixed column of volunteers and levies drawn from several commanderies, with men from the central plain as its core and southern commandery troops serving as guides and fill; what can be certain is that it was large enough to march in divided columns, to hold heights and to conduct siege operations at the same time, since anything smaller could not have covered that line within a year. The rebels are equally unnumbered: commandery troops formed the backbone, with armed local Yue bands attached, numerous enough to hold heights and block waterways behind stockades and also numerous enough to be beaten in the open field. Casualties and captures differ from source to source and cannot be checked; what is certain is that Li Zhi was executed, that Chen Tao's following broke up with him, that the Jiaozhou commanderies submitted one after another, and that the result of the war took the form of a number of leaders killed and a number of men surrendered rather than of one annihilating battle. Administratively, the local institutions of the five commanderies of Jiaozhi, Yulin, Guilin, Nanhai and Hepu were reconnected to the court after the war, and the counties, post-stations, military farms and garrison posts were restored accordingly; Hepu and Nanhai were then important salt districts, and salt and rice were the supplies on which the expedition depended most along the coastal stretch.
cause: 直接導火線是建武十六年秋交趾校尉李贄與陳濤的舉兵：他們殺死交趾太守，郡兵隨反，數郡先後響應，一場以郡兵為骨幹的地方反亂在數月之內成形。但反亂背後是更長的結構性矛盾。交州自武帝平南越後置郡，其治所與內地的聯繫主要靠一條沿海航運線和一位又一位由內地派任、對越地陌生的太守；郡吏與越人豪酋之間既有合作，也有爭奪賦役與資源的摩擦。光武帝在開國之初削地方兵權、收郡縣之兵，本意是收兵於朝廷，落在交趾的郡兵身上，卻削掉了地方勢力最倚重的那一塊。於是當朝廷的收編與郡兵的既有利益正面相撞時，反亂的號召不需要多少宣傳就能奏效。沿海航運又使交趾同時是邊陲與海上通道：合浦、南海通往交趾的船路一旦被叛軍控制，沿海各郡就難以自守。漢廷的應變能力在這裡暴露無遺——交州沒有常備大軍，郡兵分散守土，必須由中原本部遠征；而在詔書下達之前，中樞也曾討論是否先遣使招撫、給郡兵改過的機會，最終還是選擇以兵威掃平，於是有了馬援這支自湘鄉出發、沿湘江直下的遠征軍。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the rising of the Jiaozhi commandant Li Zhi and Chen Tao in the autumn of the sixteenth year of Jianwu: they killed the Administrator of Jiaozhi, the commandery troops followed, several commanderies answered in turn, and within a few months a local rebellion with commandery soldiers as its backbone had taken shape. Behind it lay a longer structural tension. Since the Emperor Wu had pacified the south and created commanderies there, Jiaozhou had been tied to the interior chiefly by a single coastal shipping line and by a succession of administrators posted from the interior who knew little of the Yue country; friction between commandery clerks and the local Yue chieftains over tribute, corvée and resources ran alongside cooperation. Guangwu's policy of taking the commanderies' arms into the centre at the beginning of the dynasty meant well in principle, but in Jiaozhi it cut away precisely the thing the local power most relied on. When the court's take-over met the commandery troops' existing interests head-on, the call to revolt needed little persuasion to take hold. Coastal shipping also made Jiaozhi a frontier and a maritime channel at once: once the ships of Hepu and Nanhai were in the insurgents' hands, the coastal commanderies could not hold themselves. The court's response exposed the weakness of the whole arrangement — Jiaozhou had no standing army, its commandery troops were dispersed and tied to their own districts, and troops had to be brought from the central plain. Even before the edict went out, the central government debated whether to send envoys first and give the commandery soldiers a chance to surrender; in the end it chose to settle the matter by force, and so there was Ma Yuan's expedition, leaving Xiangxiang and descending the Xiang River.
impact: 最深遠的後果是交州重新納入朝廷的郡縣體系，並且這一次接入的方式改變了東漢在南疆的統治結構：不再是靠幾個據點和一個軍事鎮守維繫，而是郡縣、屯田與鎮兵三者合一，常備的邊防力量由中央調來的軍隊、地方屯田的糧食與郡縣的行政共同組成。南北的水路也因這次用兵被打通：湘江—漓江—珠江—交趾這條線從此穩定通行，合浦、南海的鹽與海外貿易得以延續，漢代海上絲路的南段由此維持。北部的楚地、嶺南的越地與後來的南中地區，在制度與物質上被拉進同一個循環，銅鼓與漢式墓葬在嶺南的出現，反映的正是郡縣深入與漢越交融的過程。對馬援個人而言，此役是他平生最完整的一次遠征，功成之後拜大將軍、封新豐侯，「大丈夫當立功異域」的話也因而成為中國史書中最有代表性的遠征敘事；他在建武二十五年去世，身後有人進讒，詔令史官為之立傳，《後漢書·馬援傳》於是成為本戰最重要的史料。反過來看，這場勝仗也留下隱憂：武力平定只能壓住一時的叛亂，並不能消除邊郡治理的結構問題，交州其後仍屢有變亂，說明遠征買來的是時間，而不是制度性的答案。
impactEn: The most far-reaching consequence was that Jiaozhou was drawn back into the commandery system of the court, and the way it was drawn back altered the shape of Eastern Han rule in the far south. It was no longer a matter of a few fortified posts and one military garrison; county administration, military farms and stationed troops were combined, and the permanent frontier was carried by an expeditionary force sent from the centre, by the grain of local farms and by the administration of the commanderies together. The north-south water route was also opened by this campaign: the line from the Xiang through the Li and Zhu rivers to Jiaozhi became a regularly used road, the salt of Hepu and Nanhai and the overseas trade that depended on it went on, and the southern stretch of the Han maritime silk road was kept alive by it. Chu lands in the north, Yue lands in Lingnan and the later regions of Nanzhong were drawn into one circuit of institutions and goods, and the appearance of bronze drums and Han-style tombs in Lingnan records precisely that process of commanderies pushing inward and Han and Yue blending together. For Ma Yuan himself the campaign was the most complete of his expeditions; he rose to General-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinfeng, and the saying about a great man earning his achievement in a distant land entered the histories as the most representative account of far-off campaigns the Chinese historical record has. He died in the twenty-fifth year of Jianwu; there were accusations against him after his death, and an edict ordered the historiographers to write his biography, which is why the Biography of Ma Yuan in the History of the Later Han is the most important source for this war. The reverse side of the victory is a warning: military suppression can hold down a rebellion for a time but cannot remove the structural faults of frontier administration, and disturbances continued to break out in Jiaozhou afterwards. The expedition bought time, not a lasting institutional answer.
result: 建武十七年（公元41年），交趾平定。李贄伏誅，陳濤所部潰散，鬱林、桂林、南海、合浦各郡相繼歸附，交州重歸朝廷版籍，這場由郡兵和越人諸部掀起的地方反亂至此結束。善後工作隨之展開：被戰事破壞的縣、亭、郵驛與屯田逐一恢復，郡兵與鎮兵重新配置，郡吏與將士分赴各縣，一批交趾的吏員、降附部眾與被徙之地的人口被安置到荊州、零陵一帶，以充實西南邊郡的屯田人手與兵源（此事的具體名籍與人數，各家記載互有出入，已不可考）。馬援的軍隊隨即班師，朝廷論功行賞，他後來又平定羌亂、封新豐侯，最終在建武二十五年去世。從大局看，結果是雙重的：漢朝在嶺南的統治恢復並且換了一種更牢固的形態，交州在此後近兩百年裡一直是王朝在南方的邊郡與前哨，直到孫吳據有交州、三國鼎立的局面成形；而作為代價，遠征軍走過的這條線上消耗掉的糧秣、患病的人數與無法追回的傷亡，都沒有留下可以核對的數目，只留下馬援傳記裡那幾段簡略的文字。
resultEn: In the seventeenth year of Jianwu, in 41 AD, Jiaozhi was pacified. Li Zhi was executed, Chen Tao's following broke up, Yulin, Guilin, Nanhai and Hepu submitted one after another, and the local rising of the commandery troops and the Yue bands came to an end with Jiaozhou restored to the registers of the court. The aftermath followed: the counties, post-stations, courier stations and military farms broken by the fighting were restored one by one; commandery troops and garrison troops were redeployed; commandery clerks and soldiers were sent to their posts; and a number of Jiaozhi officials, surrendered bands and people moved out of the country were settled in the Jingzhou and Lingling regions to supply the military farms and the manpower of the southwestern border commanderies. The particulars of those transfers, in name and in number, differ from source to source and can no longer be checked. Ma Yuan's army then marched home, the court rewarded the service according to merit, and he subsequently pacified the Qiang, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinfeng, and died in the twenty-fifth year of Jianwu. Seen whole, the outcome was double. Han rule in Lingnan was restored and took on a more durable shape, and Jiaozhou remained the dynasty's southern frontier commandery and outpost for nearly two centuries afterwards, until the situation of the Three Kingdoms formed around Sun Wu's occupation of Jiaozhou. And the cost was the grain, the sick and the unrecoverable dead of the line the army walked, none of which left a figure that can be verified — only the few plain sentences that survive in Ma Yuan's biography.
